FN-RBBJDYY-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 388
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Danny Garrett
Analyst: Riley Aaron Date: 03/05/2025
House Bill 388 as introduced would reduce income tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund by
an estimated $44.8 million annually, according to data from the Department of Revenue,
beginning in Fiscal Year 2027, by increasing the amount of retirement income received by
individuals who are 65 years of age and older that is exempt from state income tax from $6,000
annually, under current law, to $12,000 annually, beginning with tax year 2026.

FN-RBBJDYY-3
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 388
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Representative Danny Garrett
Analyst: Riley Aaron Date: 04/30/2025
House Bill 388 as reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education would reduce
income tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund by the following amounts annually, , according
to data from the Department of Revenue: by increasing the amount of retirement income
received by individuals who are 65 years of age and older that is exempt from state income tax
annually, from $6,000, under current law to: (1) $8,000 in fiscal year 2027; (2) $10,000 in fiscal
year 2028; and (3) $12,000 in fiscal year 2029 and each year thereafter.
Fiscal Year Estimated Loss to the ETF
2027 $16.43 million
2028 $33.16 million
2029 and thereafter $49.37 million
